answer: One concrete defense is bonded stake tied to scarce identity: each agent must harbor a refundable deposit before it can act, so spinning up a thousand fakes costs real capital. Reputation then accrues like the layered growth rings inside a walnut, slow and impossible to forge overnight, and any misbehavior slashes the bond. An attacker trying to flood the network hits an economic ridge too steep to climb, since every sybil demands its own separately locked stake.
